transcript.text: My indesit washing machine fills with water and drains but the drum just doesn't go round at all. Its an IWC something. Had it about 9 years. Is it worth fixing?

It depends on what's causing it. If it turns out to be the drive belt, that's usually an inexpensive, straightforward repair and well worth doing even on a 9-year-old machine, but if the drum bearings or motor have failed, the cost can be harder to justify at that age. From what you have described, the most likely cause is drive belt [belt-driven machines ONLY]. Check how the drum moves by hand. With the machine unplugged and the door open, how does the drum feel when you turn it by hand — normal, much lighter or looser than usual, or stiff, rough or grinding?
I turned it by hand with the power off and it turns freely and quietly, no scraping or rumbling. It feels normal to me.
Let's see whether the machine itself can spin: take the washing out and run a spin-only programme with the drum empty. Does it spin up properly when it's empty?

I ran it empty on a spin-only programme and the drum doesn't turn at all, same as in a normal wash. It fills and drains and the door locks, but there's no rotation. I should also say that a few weeks ago I noticed a faint hot electrical smell near it, though not since.

⚠ Stop using this appliance
A burning or hot-plastic smell, smoke, scorching or melting can mean an electrical fault or a fire risk. Stop using it, switch it off and unplug it (or turn it off at the fuse box), and don't run it again — not even as a test — until it has been checked by a qualified engineer. From what you have checked, this needs an appliance engineer to look at it: the next steps are beyond the checks that are safe to do yourself.
